RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 complete) — CONFIRMED, defect (latent), classification: design-invariant violation / codec seam never wired into the comment differ.

ROOT CAUSE (proven): outbound_comments._diff_comments derives its two dedup keys through DIFFERENT transformations, and the local-side key never passes through the codec's outbound content normalization that the send path's landed form embodies.
- Jira-side key = decode(stored wire form): outbound_comments.py:296 -> _normalize_comment_body (py:113) -> inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text (inbound_fields.py:134-146: ADF dict -> adf_to_text; str -> pass-through).
- Local-side key = fit_comment(marker-strip(str(raw))): outbound_comments.py:314 — truncation ONLY, no normalize_outbound. Mismatch re-emits at outbound_comments.py:319, every pass, forever.
- The description path composes the protection the comment path lacks: outbound_mapper.py:77 normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(v)) — send value is its own round-trip fixed point — and the differ compares exactly that value (outbound_field_diff.py:277-292; reconcile_check.py:194-198). Pinned by test_rich_text_seam_heldout.py:48.

MECHANISM: for any codec/converter whose outbound content transform is not the identity, the body Jira stores decodes to normalize_outbound(sent) while the local key stays the raw text; membership test at outbound_comments.py:315 fails, the differ re-emits the already-mirrored comment, and each new copy stores the SAME transformed form, so it never converges (no self-heal).

WHY LATENT TODAY (verified): Cloud send is acli_cli_ops.add_comment (py:479) = truncation only, rebar computes no ADF for comments; DC WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound is identity (rich_text.py:96). Whether ACLI's own text->ADF rejoins soft wraps remains an OPEN live question — if it does, this is firing on Cloud now.

DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENTS (unit-level, real _diff_comments + real inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text + real Cloud fit_comment; simulated store; no live Jira):
- Fixture: local body 'first line of prose\nsoft-wrapped continuation' — rebar's own adf.text_to_adf (py:275) rejoins soft wraps, so decode(encode(v)) != v.
- E1 (H1 true): pass 1 emits the add; simulate a transforming send (store = text_to_adf(sanitized sent body)); pass 2 RE-EMITS the mirrored comment (1 mutation); pass 3 with both stored copies STILL re-emits — H4 'self-heals' REJECTED. Keys: jira='first line of prose soft-wrapped continuation' vs local='first line of prose\nsoft-wrapped continuation' — divergence is exactly the soft-wrap rejoin.
- E2 (H3 rejected — latency proven): identical cycle but store preserves text verbatim (hardBreak ADF, and DC plain-string): 0 mutations both — dedup converges today; also proves the RECONCILER_MARKER strip is not a confound.
- E3 (H2 rejected — asymmetry real): same fixture as a description through OutboundFieldMapper(AdfCodec()): send value == decode(encode(send value)) — fixed point, converges.
- E4 (the missing half named): routing the local key through AdfCodec().normalize_outbound first makes it equal the Jira-side key.
- Existing suite green (19 passed: test_outbound_differ_comment_dedup.py, test_diff_comments_adf.py, test_rich_text_seam_heldout.py) — every current dedup test uses round-trip-identity fixtures, so this cell is genuinely untested.

AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES (defect, not not-a-bug): the convergence invariant is documented and enforced for every OTHER transform on this exact key derivation — truncation guard at outbound_comments.py:307-313 ('apply the SAME shared truncation... otherwise... re-emits forever', bug 6afc), DC parity pin backend.py:239-243 ('MUST stay byte-identical... or the loop never converges'), description composition comment outbound_mapper.py:63-82, and prior fixed same-class bugs 85a1/1f3d/4292. The normalization half of the same rule is the un-paired remainder.

SIBLING CANDIDATES (same send-value/compare-key asymmetry class; named, not filed):
1. _map_comments_for_create (outbound_comments.py:80) — create-path comments land through the same transforming send; next-pass dedup of those bodies hits this same broken key (same mechanism, second entry point).
2. Title/summary compare (outbound_field_diff.py:266-271, outbound_mapper 'summary'=raw value): compare key is the raw local title guarded only by _text_matches rstrip (py:49-54); any remote summary content transform beyond trailing whitespace reopens the identical shape. Latent-latent; name only.
3. The inbound comment mirror is ID-bound (inbound_differ.py:299-346, jira_comment_id) — protected by identity binding, NOT a sibling; noted as the contrast case.
4. The codec-law gap itself: no test pins normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) for RichTextCodec impls (rich_text.py:43/96, rich_text_codec.py) — a pandoc WikiTextCodec violating it would pass today's suite (ticket AC #4).

PHASE-2 SKETCH: expose the codec's outbound normalization to the comment differ through the ticket-21ca injection seam (extend the injected sanitizer port — e.g. FieldSanitizer.normalize_comment -> codec.normalize_outbound; Cloud: adf.normalize_description, DC: identity) and derive the local key as the composition the SEND path actually lands (mirror the send order: decorate/truncate-then-normalize, marker-strip after — get the order right the way outbound_mapper.py:63-82 documents fit-before-normalize, and pin it with a heldout composition test like test_rich_text_seam_heldout.py:48). Jira-side key unchanged (already decode). Also pin the codec law normalize_outbound(t)==decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) per impl, plus a corpus fixed-point property test over real comment bodies (AC #3/#4), and document the symmetric-degradation invariant (AC #5).

SUGGESTED RED ORACLE (fails today at outbound_comments.py:314-319): unit test in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/ — given an injected sanitizer/codec whose outbound transform is NOT identity (soft-wrap rejoin) and a Jira snapshot holding exactly what that send path stores for the local comment (decorated, truncated, encoded via text_to_adf), _diff_comments emits ZERO adds. Today it emits one (E1b). Negative control: the E2 verbatim-store cell stays zero-mutation.

Experiments were run from throwaway scripts (removed); no tracked file was modified. Phase 2 not started per session scope.

## THE SEAM IS UP — Gerrit 1329. Read what it does and does NOT change carefully.

`_diff_comments` now composes its local comparison key as
`codec.normalize_outbound(sanitizer.fit_comment(body))` — **fit-then-normalize, the same order
`outbound_mapper.map_fields_to_remote` uses for descriptions.** Injected via a `codec` parameter
mirroring the existing `_resolve_inbound_mapper` / `_resolve_sanitizer` seam.

### PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED TODAY, and that is deliberate — but be precise about it

The parameter defaults to `_IdentityCodec`, and **nothing wires a real codec into
`compute_outbound_mutations`** — verified: `grep codec outbound_differ.py` returns nothing. So the
key reduces to exactly `sanitizer.fit_comment(body)`, today's existing formula. Every existing
protection (truncation guard, marker strip, whitespace strip) behaves byte-identically.

That is the right scope *now*, and the reason is worth stating: rebar applies NO content
transformation on the comment send path — Cloud comments go out through ACLI as
`--body <text>` and ACLI's own conversion is opaque to us; DC's `WikiTextCodec` is pure identity.
There is no real codec to inject yet. **So AC1 is met STRUCTURALLY — the key now routes through the
codec seam — but the latent bug is DISARMED BY CONSTRUCTION rather than fixed-and-proven.** When
pandoc or any Markdown-aware encoder lands, injecting the real codec is a one-line change and the
new cells prove it converges.

Do not read this ticket as "comment dedup is now correct under conversion". Read it as "the seam and
the proof exist, so conversion can land without re-discovering this".

### The convergence argument, which is the part that matters

The Jira-side key was and remains `decode_inbound(<wire body>)`. The local key is now
`normalize_outbound(fit(local))`. The codec law `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`
— **now PINNED by a new test for BOTH `AdfCodec` and `WikiTextCodec`** — makes those equal once a
real codec is wired into a send path where `to_wire(fit(local))` is what Jira stores. Same
fixed-point argument that already protects descriptions.

### Evidence

RED first, verbatim: 8 of 9 new cells failed with
`TypeError: _diff_comments() got an unexpected keyword argument 'codec'`. The ninth passed by
design — the "no codec injected, baseline unchanged" negative control, which needed no new code and
is what proves the default path is untouched.

The missing cell now exists and uses the REAL `AdfCodec`, not a stub: a non-identity codec plus an
already-mirrored comment must emit ZERO adds. Plus the counter-regression (a genuinely new comment
is still emitted — the too-lax direction), and an idempotence property over soft-wrapped prose, code
fences, bullets, emphasis, literal pipes and backticks.

Gates: ruff clean, mypy 421, hygiene 0, **2161 passed** across unit + integration.
`outbound_comments.py` 407/800.

### A NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING

The implementer's editing tool was briefly pointed at the SHARED main checkout
(`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar`) instead of its isolated worktree — the checkout AGENTS.md and
CLAUDE.local.md single out as possibly holding uncommitted operator WIP. It caught this itself
before running anything and restored the file.

**I verified the restore independently rather than accepting the report**: `git status --short` in
that checkout is EMPTY, `outbound_comments.py` is byte-identical to HEAD, and no stray test file
exists. Nothing was lost. But it was clean only because there happened to be no WIP there at the
time — that is luck, not process. Worth knowing that an isolated-worktree agent can still reach the
shared checkout if its tooling is not scoped.

# The comment dedup key is NOT normalized the way the description send value is

## Summary

The description path and the comment path have different convergence protections, and the missing
piece is exactly the normalization half. Today this is LATENT — it costs nothing, because rebar does
not currently model any content transformation on the comment send path. Any real Markdown/wiki
converter activates it, and the symptom is duplicate Jira comments re-posted on every pass, forever.

Filed from a peer session's round-trip experiment over 5,568 real rebar bodies, verified here
against the code rather than taken on report.

## The asymmetry, in code

**Descriptions are protected.** `adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.map_fields_to_remote` composes

    normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))

so the value sent is already its own fixed point under the round trip. The ordering is deliberate and
documented in a long comment there, and it is PINNED by
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_seam_heldout.py::test_cloud_send_path_composition_is_unchanged`,
which includes an explicitly soft-wrapped case.

**Comments are not.** `outbound_comments._diff_comments` builds its comparison key with

    compare_body = sanitizer.fit_comment(_normalize_comment_body(raw))

There is no `normalize_outbound` equivalent. And `_normalize_comment_body` does NOT normalize both
sides the same way — it calls `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`, which is:

    if isinstance(body, dict):  return adf_to_text(body)     # the JIRA side: decoded
    return str(body) if body is not None else ""             # the LOCAL side: pass-through

So the Jira side is decoded and the local side is handed back verbatim. The two sides are compared
after DIFFERENT transformations.

## Why the truncation guard proves the shape of the bug

The comment path already carries one guard of exactly this kind, added after it bit:

> the send path truncates an over-length body ... Apply the SAME shared truncation to the expected
> local body before the membership test; otherwise the full local body never matches the truncated
> Jira body and the diff re-emits forever.

That is the identical failure mode, patched for the ONE transformation the send path was known to
apply. Nothing generalizes it. A content transformation gets no such treatment, and the machinery
that would notice — a comparison against what Jira will actually store — does not exist.

The `_EXCLUDED_COMMENT_PREFIXES` canary exclusion is a second instance of the same class patched
per-symptom: a volatile timestamp never matches a prior body, so the comment re-added every pass.

## Why it is latent RIGHT NOW (do not "fix" a bug that is not firing)

Cloud comments go out through ACLI as `jira workitem comment create --body <text>`
(`acli_cli_ops.add_comment`). rebar never computes the ADF that Jira will store, so it applies no
content transformation of its own, and the dedup key happens to match. DC's `WikiTextCodec` is pure
identity in all four operations, so DC transforms nothing either.

I could not establish whether ACLI's own text→ADF conversion alters bodies (e.g. rejoining soft
wraps) — that is a live question about a third-party binary and only a live pass settles it. If it
DOES, this is already firing on Cloud today. Empirically, rebar's own `text_to_adf` DOES rejoin soft
wraps, so the transformation is not hypothetical for that encoder.

## What I verified empirically (so the future work is not built on a wrong premise)

Probing today's `adf.normalize_description` directly: `**/*.py`, `__pycache__`, `**a** **b**`, pipe
tables, backticks, fenced blocks, `-`/`*` bullets and `__bold__` all round-trip BYTE-IDENTICALLY and
are fixed points. Today's ADF path does no Markdown parsing at all — it only rejoins soft wraps and
strips trailing whitespace. So the peer session's 9-19% flap rate is a property of the PROPOSED
converter, not of anything shipping.

## The good news: the seam is already in the right place

`map_fields_to_remote` is SHARED and composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(...))` for both
backends, so a pandoc-backed `WikiTextCodec` slots in by implementing the codec — no differ change.
The `RichTextCodec` four-operation split is what makes that possible. This ticket is about the
comment path catching up to the description path, not about redesigning the seam.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the comment dedup key is computed from what the SEND PATH will produce, the same way the
      description value is — i.e. the local comparison key goes through the codec's outbound
      normalization, not just `fit_comment`
- [ ] a test asserts the property directly: given a codec whose outbound transform is NOT the
      identity, a local comment already mirrored in Jira emits NO add. This is the cell that does
      not exist today — every current dedup test uses transformations applied to both sides
- [ ] a corpus/property test over real rebar comment bodies asserts encode-then-decode is a fixed
      point for the comment path, not just unit examples
- [ ] `RichTextCodec` implementations are pinned to `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`.
      `WikiTextCodec`'s identity satisfies this trivially TODAY, which is why a pandoc implementation
      that got it wrong would pass the existing suite
- [ ] the dependency is DOCUMENTED: outbound has no origin-aware gate, and the reason it does not
      need one is that degradation is symmetric. If encode ever stops being decode's inverse, a body
      pulled from Jira starts being re-emitted and the human's Jira-native formatting is destroyed.
      That invariant is currently load-bearing and unwritten
compiled_state.title: Comment dedup key is not normalized the way the description send value is
